name: Joshua
role: Moses' successor, who led Israel into Canaan
whenBasis: 1 Kings 6:1 puts the exodus 480 years before Solomon's fourth year, ≈1446 BC; many historians put it under Ramesses II, ≈1270s–1250s BC. The text gives no date in a calendar we can fix.
summary: Son of Nun, of Ephraim, Moses' assistant, who led Israel against Amalek and went with Moses up the mountain of God. One of the two spies who trusted the LORD, he was commissioned to succeed Moses. He led the people across the Jordan, took Jericho and Ai, fought the kings of the south and north, divided the land among the tribes, and before he died at 110 called them to choose whom they would serve.
body: Moses renames him from Hoshea to Joshua, which means the LORD saves. He fights Amalek while Moses holds up his hands, stays in the tent of meeting after Moses leaves, and, with Caleb, pleads with the people to trust the LORD after the spies' report. Moses lays hands on him before Eleazar.

After Moses' death the LORD tells him to be strong and courageous. The Jordan stops while the priests with the ark stand in it; a commander of the LORD's army meets him near Jericho; the walls fall at the shout. After defeat at Ai for Achan's sin, he takes it. At Gibeon he asks the sun to stand still. He takes the land and divides it by lot.
In old age he gathers the tribes at Shechem, recounts what the LORD has done since Abraham, and says, “As for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.” He is buried at Timnath-serah in Ephraim.

moments.text: The commander of the LORD's army

later.text: Kathleen Kenyon's excavations at Tell es-Sultan (1952–58) dated the destruction of Jericho's last walled city to ≈1550 BC and found little of a town in the following centuries, which fits neither date of the conquest easily. Bryant Wood (1990) re-dated the destruction to ≈1400 BC. Most archaeologists follow Kenyon.
